quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Front and rear brakes have equal stopping power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides most of the stopping power — about 70 percent. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Stay out of the center of the lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: On a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit riding to six hours per day and rest at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants — they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need?
questions.correctAnswerText: The same as cars
questions.explanation: In traffic, motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots
Encourage other drivers to share your lane
Give you a way to escape from danger

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from blind spots, wind, and hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route if needed.

questions.question: To swerve quickly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward where you want to go
Press the handgrip away from where you want to go

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward where you want to go
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: In ideal conditions, what is the minimum safe following distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, maintain at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for group riding. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. The left side is too close to the passing driver. The right side may make them return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, riding on the far side of the lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check side mirrors
Is recommended because a passenger can alert the driver
Is illegal because you must ride in the center

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check side mirrors
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When preparing a passenger to ride, which instruction should you NOT give?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to sit close to you, not far away. They should sit as far forward as they can, hold the handholds or your waist, and keep their legs away from hot and moving parts.

questions.question: When you are stopped, what gear should you be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: First gear
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake lights before you slow down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake lights before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake lights before slowing down. The tailgater may not see upcoming hazards. A warning gives them time to react.

questions.question: What percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking?
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes and deaths. Studies show that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle accidents had been drinking.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply steady pressure to the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. Use more front brake as weight moves forward. Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually, reduce your lean, then brake harder.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil that makes it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve. Only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time. Do not brake and swerve together, as this may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press the front brake hard to keep the front tire from locking.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down safely. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Your clothes should also give you extra protection in case of a crash. Chapped lips are not protected by clothing.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change positions based on different conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change positions based on different conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you ride based on what helps drivers see you and gives you space around you.

questions.question: Who sets the pace when riding in a group?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they do not have to rush to catch up, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.
